### Keypad and Keyboard
On-screen keys that type into a text field: a PIN or dial pad, or a full keyboard.

Component ID: `keypad`

[Component documentation](https://www.expressivecss.com/keypad.html.md) · [Repository source](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/blob/master/docs/src/pages/keypad.astro) · [Matching tag](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/tree/v0.15.0)

Contract: ExpressiveCSS 0.15.0

Contract SHA-256: `c94b2ef56807cf2fdb57c9d9c34f28aaf95ad75a16f409baedf7e684cb42ed58`

#### Selection and adaptation

Runtime ownership: `auto-init`. No dedicated entry in the reviewed Google component inventory.

Example: A café kiosk asks for a four-digit loyalty PIN with a keypad under a password field. A checkout form on a phone uses a text field with inputmode="numeric" instead.

#### Material mapping

Relationship: none. Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

Upstream: web-extension-inventory-reviewed (2026-10-11); [evidence](https://m3.material.io/components).

Requirements and boundaries: design reference web-extensions-review. The inventory page renders client-side, so this review relies on the 2026-09-13 inventory review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.

Support (2026-10-11, `llm.md#keypad-and-keyboard`): A three-column keypad of round keys with two-cell wide keys and a keyboard of rows sized from a column count with an optional number row, typing into the field named by aria-controls with value keys, Backspace, Enter, a one-shot Shift, data-key keys inside the field's wrapper, dial-pad letters, styled call keys, an onKey callback and a pressed shape morph.

Web adaptation: Keys are native buttons in a named group; edits go through the field's value and fire a composed input event, Enter uses requestSubmit() so validation runs, and inputmode="none" on the field keeps the device keyboard closed. Browsers check minlength only on what a person types, so the keypad checks it on its own edits.

Known boundary: Typing at the caret, maxlength, pattern validation on Enter, Backspace including emoji, Enter submitting a form and adding a new line in a textarea, a one-shot Shift with capitals shown, Caps Lock, Layer keys, hardware key highlight, minlength on keypad edits, number inputs, disabled fieldsets, in-field keys, shadow roots, focus staying in the field, the keypad grid and wide keys, keyboard key widths and the number row, the pressed shape and destroy are checked in a browser; screen reader output, forced colors, enlarged text and touch devices remain unverified. There is no caps lock, no symbol layer switching and no hardware key highlighting, and minlength does not apply to keypad edits; the page owns layouts beyond the keys it writes.

Full parity remains unassessed. [Capability evidence](../references/capability-roadmap.md#keypad).

#### Contract

A `.keypad` is three columns of round 72dp keys for PINs, codes and amounts. A `.keyboard` is a surface of rows, each child a row of keys, for text. Both are a `role="group"` with an `aria-label`, and `aria-controls` names the `<input>` or `<textarea>` they type into. Every key is a `<button type="button">`. A key with a `value` types it at the caret, replacing any selection, and the field gets the same `input` event typing would fire. `AutoInit()` starts every `.keypad` and `.keyboard`.

#### Syntax

```html
<div class="field outlined">
  <input id="pin" type="password" inputmode="none" maxlength="6" placeholder=" " autocomplete="off">
  <label for="pin">PIN</label>
</div>

<div class="keypad" role="group" aria-label="PIN keypad" aria-controls="pin">
  <button type="button" value="1">1</button>
  <button type="button" value="2">2</button>
  <!-- … 3 to 9 … -->
  <span></span>
  <button type="button" value="0">0</button>
  <button type="button" data-key="Backspace" aria-label="Delete">
    <span class="material-symbols" aria-hidden="true">backspace</span>
  </button>
</div>

<div class="keyboard" role="group" aria-label="Keyboard" aria-controls="message">
  <div class="numbers"><button type="button" value="1">1</button><!-- … 2 to 0 … --></div>
  <div><button type="button" value="q">q</button><!-- … --></div>
  <div><!-- a to l --></div>
  <div>
    <button type="button" data-key="Shift" aria-pressed="false" aria-label="Shift">
      <span class="material-symbols" aria-hidden="true">shift</span>
    </button>
    <!-- z to m -->
    <button type="button" data-key="Backspace" aria-label="Delete">
      <span class="material-symbols" aria-hidden="true">backspace</span>
    </button>
  </div>
  <div>
    <button type="button" value=" " aria-label="Space"></button>
    <button type="button" data-key="Enter" aria-label="New line">
      <span class="material-symbols" aria-hidden="true">keyboard_return</span>
    </button>
  </div>
</div>
```

#### Options

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onKey` | Function | `null` | Called after every key press with the text typed or the function key's name (`'Backspace'`, `'Enter'`, `'Shift'`, `'CapsLock'`, `'Layer'`). Works without `aria-controls`. |
| `i18n.tooShort` | Function | `(minLength) => 'Use at least ' + minLength + ' characters.'` | The validation message for a keypad-typed value shorter than the field's `minlength`. |

#### Methods

- `.destroy()`: Stops the keypad typing. The shared listeners on the document or shadow root go with the last keypad there.

#### Also documented

The Keypad and Keyboard section of the [API reference](https://www.expressivecss.com/llm.md) also covers Tokens, Properties.

#### Rules

- `keypad-is-group`: A keypad or keyboard is a set of related keys. Give it role="group" and an aria-label so its keys are announced together.
- `keypad-is-labelled`: Name the keypad or keyboard with aria-label, for example "PIN keypad".
- `keypad-key-type`: A <button> inside a form defaults to type=submit, so every key would submit it. Give each key type="button".
